text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm seeing a weird 429 pattern on a low-throughput route. Sporadic users get 429s even though we should be well under per-route QPS. Anyone seen this with sparse traffic?

raj: Yup. Cold-start + burst windows can look like sudden spikes. Which headers/body do you see on the 429s?

maria: Example response we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:/v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json

{ "error": "rate_limited", "soft": true }
```
Note: no Retry-After header, and our Node SDK's auto-retry ended up hammering then surfacing a 429 to the client.

sam: Hosted or Dedicated?

maria: Hosted (us-west), per-route quota is 50/min but traffic is super sparse (single requests every few minutes). SDK did default retry and client saw a 429 then a delayed 200.

raj: That tracks — we have a "burst window" where token accounting is weird after long idle. The first request after idle can consume perceived tokens and trigger a soft 429. We should make header semantics explicit for soft vs hard 429s.

alice: SDK note: current Node SDK treats any 429 as retryable when `retryOnRateLimit` is true. We rely on `Retry-After` if present, otherwise exponential backoff. If the service omits Retry-After, clients behave inconsistently. We should standardize.

maria: Agreed. Part of the problem here is missing headers. We saw a response with no Retry-After and `X-RateLimit-Bucket` was present but sometimes empty/null.

ci-bot: deploy: hosted-api v2.3.4 rolled @ 2026-02-10 15:04 UTC :rocket:

raj: Proposal: require `Retry-After` on any quota-induced 429 (soft or hard). Add an explicit `X-RateLimit-Type: soft|hard` header for clarity, and keep backward-compatible `X-RateLimit-Remaining`/`X-RateLimit-Bucket`. Also consider `X-RateLimit-Parent-Bucket` when route uses shared pool.

sam: +1. SDK should implement prefer-Retry-After logic and fall back to expo-backoff with jitter. Suggest default cap: 4 retries, base 200ms, max delay ~2s with jitter. Document in changelog.

alice: 👍 I'll add logic in SDK to: 1) prefer `Retry-After` (seconds), 2) if missing, use expo backoff with jitter, 3) expose `retryOnRateLimit` toggle. I'll add tests for sparse-traffic scenarios.

sam: SRE suggestion: emit a metric when `X-RateLimit-Type` is missing on 429 responses so we can detect old/rogue nodes.

maria: Quick question — for per-route quotas that are actually carved from a shared pool, will we expose the parent bucket so clients can understand why they hit a limit?

raj: Yes — header plan is to add `X-RateLimit-Parent-Bucket: pool:write-heavy` when applicable. That will be in the RFC.

maria: Perfect. Can someone own the API header change and put example responses in the RFC? That will help me update client retry logic. @raj?

raj: I'll own it. I'll update the rate-limit RFC with examples (soft/hard 429s, Retry-After mandatory for quota blocks, example `X-RateLimit-Type`, and `X-RateLimit-Parent-Bucket`). Will ping this thread when done. ETA EOD.

maria: Awesome, thanks :raised_hands:

alice: Once RFC lands I'll open an SDK PR and link it here.

raj: Filed: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/rl-headers-2026 (draft) — adding examples now.

maria: Thanks everyone — will validate against the RFC and rerun client tests tomorrow morning.

sam: If you hit flakey behavior after the SDK PR, ping #eng-sre and we'll sweep infra config. :eyes:
